name: magnetic-sector-180
description: Closed form: t = 15 mm / v + pi m / (|q| B). A hard-edge 0.5 T magnet fills x > 0 (a region with no fringe - the sharp cut-off of first-order beam optics). An m/z 100 cation accelerated through 1 kV starts 5 mm in front of the edge going +x, drifts in, turns through a semicircle of radius r = m v / (|q| B) = 91.057 mm, leaves the edge 2r = 182.114 mm away going -x, and drifts 10 mm back to the detector plane x = -10 mm. It is launched away from its detector, which the validator accepts because a magnet can turn an ion round although it does no work on it. The 15 mm of straight flight is taken as an exact field-free drift and the magnet is integrated, so the example checks both that the drift stops at the magnet's face and that the ion lands on that face. With B ignored the ion never comes back. B is declared in millitesla (500 mT) to exercise the unit; the expectation is arithmetic this engine had no part in.
